/-!
# Relative projective coordinate charts

A normalized homogeneous coordinate family over a field defines a morphism to
relative projective space and a canonical factor through the chart where the
normalizing coordinate is nonzero.  The corresponding affine-space map is a
closed immersion as soon as the remaining coordinates algebra-generate the
source ring.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.Coordinates

variable {k B J : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- The structural morphism of an affine spectrum induced by its `k`-algebra
structure. -/
def specToBase : Spec (.of B) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k B))

/-- A normalized integral coordinate map paired with the structural morphism
to the base field. -/
def relativeFromSpec (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    Spec (.of B) ⟶ ℙ(J; Spec (.of k)) :=
  pullback.lift specToBase (fromSpec i c hi) (Subsingleton.elim _ _)

@[reassoc]
theorem relativeFromSpec_over (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    relativeFromSpec i c hi ≫ (ℙ(J; Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) =
      specToBase := by
  rw [ProjectiveSpace.over_eq_fst]
  exact pullback.lift_fst _ _ _

@[reassoc]
theorem relativeFromSpec_toProjInt (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    relativeFromSpec i c hi ≫ ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt J (Spec (.of k)) =
      fromSpec i c hi := by
  rw [ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt_eq_snd]
  exact pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

/-- The normalized coordinate map factored through its relative standard
chart. -/
def toAffineChartAt (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    Spec (.of B) ⟶ ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt J i (Spec (.of k)) :=
  pullback.lift (relativeFromSpec i c hi)
    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (chartHom i c hi))) (by
      rw [relativeFromSpec_toProjInt]
      rfl)

@[reassoc]
theorem toAffineChartAt_incl (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    toAffineChartAt i c hi ≫
        ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.incl J i (Spec (.of k)) =
      relativeFromSpec i c hi :=
  pullback.lift_fst _ _ _

@[reassoc]
theorem toAffineChartAt_specAway (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    toAffineChartAt i c hi ≫
        ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.toSpecAway J i (Spec (.of k)) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (chartHom i c hi)) :=
  pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

/-- The affine-space map classified by the complementary normalized
coordinates. -/
def affineSpecMap (i : J) (c : J → B) :
    Spec (.of B) ⟶ 𝔸({j : J // j ≠ i}; Spec (.of k)) :=
  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) (fun j : {j : J // j ≠ i} ↦ c j.1)).toRingHom) ≫
    (AffineSpace.SpecIso {j : J // j ≠ i} (.of k)).inv

@[reassoc]
theorem affineSpecMap_over (i : J) (c : J → B) :
    affineSpecMap (k := k) i c ≫
        (𝔸({j : J // j ≠ i}; Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) =
      specToBase := by
  rw [affineSpecMap, Category.assoc, AffineSpace.SpecIso_inv_over,
    ← Spec.map_comp]
  congr 1
  ext x
  simp

@[simp]
theorem affineSpecMap_appTop_coord (i : J) (c : J → B)
    (j : {j : J // j ≠ i}) :
    (affineSpecMap (k := k) i c).appTop
        (AffineSpace.coord (Spec (.of k)) j) =
      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv (c j.1) := by
  rw [affineSpecMap, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop]
  change (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k)
        (fun j : {j : J // j ≠ i} ↦ c j.1)).toRingHom)).appTop
        ((AffineSpace.SpecIso {j : J // j ≠ i} (.of k)).inv.appTop

  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Scheme.ΓSpecIso_inv_naturality,
    CommRingCat.comp_apply, ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom]
  exact congrArg (fun z : B ↦ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv z)
    (MvPolynomial.aeval_X
      (R := k) (fun j : {j : J // j ≠ i} ↦ c j.1) j)

/-- Algebra generation of the complementary normalized coordinates makes the
associated affine-space map a closed immersion. -/
theorem isClosedImmersion_affineSpecMap (i : J) (c : J → B)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range fun j : {j : J // j ≠ i} ↦ c j.1) = ⊤) :
    IsClosedImmersion (affineSpecMap (k := k) i c) := by
  dsimp [affineSpecMap]
  apply MorphismProperty.comp_mem @IsClosedImmersion
  · exact IsFinite.isClosedImmersion_SpecMap_aeval_of_adjoin_eq_top
      (R := k) (A := B) (n := {j : J // j ≠ i}) _ hgen
  · infer_instance

            (.of (MvPolynomial {j : J // j ≠ i} (ULift.{u} ℤ)))).inv (X j)) =

/-- The canonical projective-chart factor is the affine-space map classified
by the complementary normalized coordinates. -/
theorem toAffineChartAt_isoAffineSpace_eq_affineSpecMap
    (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1) :
    toAffineChartAt i c hi ≫
        (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.isoAffineSpace
          J i (Spec (.of k))).hom =
      affineSpecMap (k := k) i c := by
  apply AffineSpace.hom_ext
  · rw [Category.assoc,
      ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.isoAffineSpace_hom_over]
    rw [ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.over_eq,
      ← Category.assoc, toAffineChartAt_incl,
      relativeFromSpec_over, affineSpecMap_over]
  · intro j
    rw [toAffineChartAt_isoAffineSpace_appTop_coord,
      affineSpecMap_appTop_coord]

/-- If the complementary normalized coordinates algebra-generate the source
ring, the factor through the corresponding relative projective chart is a
closed immersion. -/
theorem isClosedImmersion_toAffineChartAt
    (i : J) (c : J → B) (hi : c i = 1)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin k
      (Set.range fun j : {j : J // j ≠ i} ↦ c j.1) = ⊤) :
    IsClosedImmersion (toAffineChartAt (k := k) i c hi) := by
  haveI : IsClosedImmersion
      (toAffineChartAt (k := k) i c hi ≫
        (ProjectiveSpace.affineChartAt.isoAffineSpace
          J i (Spec (.of k))).hom) := by
    rw [toAffineChartAt_isoAffineSpace_eq_affineSpecMap]
    exact isClosedImmersion_affineSpecMap i c hgen

  ⟨X, ΓSpec.adjunction.mem_essImage_of_unit_isIso _⟩

+/-! ### §3b. The leaf pushed down to the integral model `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ]`
+
+Relative projective space is by construction the base change of the integral
+model, `ℙ(n; S) = S ×_{⊤} Proj ℤ[Xᵢ]` with `ℙ(n; S) ↘ S = pullback.fst`
+(`ProjectiveSpace.over_eq_fst`), and `GeometricallyIntegral` is stable under
+base change.  So the leaf does not even depend on `k`: a *single* statement
+about the integral model discharges it over every field at once. -/
+
+open MvPolynomial in
+/-- **Geometric integrality of relative projective space from the integral
+model.**  `GeometricallyIntegral (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)` for every base scheme `S`,
+given geometric integrality of `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ] ⟶ ⊤_Scheme`.
+
+(The explicit `MorphismProperty.pullback_fst` term is required: after
+rewriting with `over_eq_fst`, plain instance search does not fire on
+mathlib's `GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.fst f g)` instance here.) -/
+theorem geometricallyIntegral_projectiveSpace_over (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u})
+    [GeometricallyIntegral (terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))))] :
+    GeometricallyIntegral (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) := by
+  rw [ProjectiveSpace.over_eq_fst]
+  exact MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _ ‹_›
+
+open MvPolynomial in
+/-- `ℙ¹_k ⟶ Spec k` is geometrically integral, given the integral model is. -/
+theorem geometricallyIntegral_p1Over
+    [GeometricallyIntegral
+      (terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))))] :
+    GeometricallyIntegral ((p1Over k).hom) :=
+  geometricallyIntegral_projectiveSpace_over _ _
+
+open MvPolynomial in
+/-- **The B3-H0 leaf, pushed all the way down to the integral model**: a
+single `k`-independent statement — `Proj ℤ[X₀, X₁] ⟶ ⊤_Scheme` is
+geometrically integral, i.e. `ℙ¹_K` is an integral scheme for every field
+`K` — discharges the field-of-constants anchor `Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k` over every
+field `k` simultaneously.
+
+This is the *whole* remaining B3-H0 frontier.  Mathlib has the analogous
+instances for **affine** space (`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean`:
+`GeometricallyIrreducible`, `GeometricallyReduced`, `GeometricallyIntegral`
+of `𝔸(n; S) ↘ S`) but nothing for `Proj`; supplying the projective analogue
+is the missing piece. -/
+theorem p1TrivialConstants_of_proj
+    [GeometricallyIntegral
+      (terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))))] :
+    P1HasTrivialConstants k :=
+  letI := geometricallyIntegral_p1Over (k := k)
+  p1_bijective_appTop_of_geometricallyIntegral
+

13	/-!
14	# Relative projective space `ℙ(n; S)`
15	
16	Mathlib v4.31 has the absolute `Proj` of a ℕ-graded ring together with the
17	properness package for `Proj.toSpecZero` (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`),
18	but no relative projective space over an arbitrary base scheme.  Following the
19	`AffineSpace` pattern (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean`) and the
20	encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment `C-0002`), this file defines
21	
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n S` (notation `ℙ(n; S)`): the relative
23	  projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by `n : Type u`, i.e.
24	  the pullback of the integral model
25	  `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n] = Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ))`
26	  along `S ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme`;
27	* the structural morphism `ℙ(n; S) ↘ S` (a `CanonicallyOver` instance) with
28	  `IsProper` (hence `IsSeparated`, `UniversallyClosed`, `LocallyOfFiniteType`,
29	  `QuasiCompact`) derived by base change from the Mathlib instances on
30	  `Proj.toSpecZero`;
31	* functoriality `ProjectiveSpace.map` in the base and the base-change square
32	  `ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map`.
33	
34	The key observations making the transfer work: the degree-zero part of the
35	homogeneous coordinate ring is the copy of `ULift ℤ` given by the constants
36	(`MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule_zero`), so `Spec (𝒜 0)` is terminal and
37	`terminal.from (Proj 𝒜)` factors as `Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜` followed by an
38	isomorphism; and for finitely many variables the coordinate ring is of finite
39	type over its degree-zero part, which is exactly the hypothesis of the Mathlib
40	properness instances.
41	
42	Blueprint: `def:projective_space`, `lem:projective_space_proper`
43	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
44	-/

8	/-!
9	# The projective line over a field, with usable charts
10	
11	We define `AlgebraicGeometry.P1 k` as `Proj` of the standard graded polynomial ring
12	`k[X₀, X₁]` (`MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k` with the degree grading), together with:
13	
14	* `P1.structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k)`, and the instance `IsProper (P1.structureMap k)`
15	  (inherited from mathlib's properness of `Proj`);
16	* the two standard affine charts `D₊(X₀)`, `D₊(X₁)` (`P1.chartOpen`), which cover `P1 k`
17	  (`P1.chartOpen_sup`), together with the open immersions `P1.chartι i` from the affine
18	  models `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`;
19	* identifications of the chart section rings with polynomial rings:
20	  `P1.awayAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[t]` (the coordinate is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`).
21	
22	The identification of the chart *overlap* with Laurent polynomials, the section-level
23	versions, and the bundled chart package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` are in the
24	continuation file `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts`.
25	
26	The generic instance `Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x)` (for a graded `R`-algebra) and
27	the lemma `LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval` (*Laurent span*: every Laurent
28	polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a polynomial in `T⁻¹`) are general-purpose
29	and live in their natural namespaces.
30	
31	## Implementation notes
32	
33	We install `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a (project-global) instance: everywhere in this
34	project, `MvPolynomial` carries the standard degree grading. Mathlib leaves this to the user
35	because other gradings exist; this project only ever uses the standard one.
36	-/

60	/-- **Laurent span**: every Laurent polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a
61	polynomial in `T⁻¹`. -/
62	theorem exists_toLaurent_add_aeval {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (f : R[T;T⁻¹]) :
63	    ∃ p q : Polynomial R, f = p.toLaurent + Polynomial.aeval (T (-1) : R[T;T⁻¹]) q := by
64	  induction f using LaurentPolynomial.induction_on' with
65	  | add p q hp hq =>
66	    obtain ⟨p₁, q₁, rfl⟩ := hp
67	    obtain ⟨p₂, q₂, rfl⟩ := hq
68	    exact ⟨p₁ + p₂, q₁ + q₂, by simp only [map_add]; ring⟩
69	  | C_mul_T n a =>
70	    rcases le_or_gt 0 n with hn | hn
71	    · refine ⟨Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ n.toNat, 0, ?_⟩
72	      rw [map_zero, add_zero, Polynomial.toLaurent_C_mul_X_pow, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hn]
73	    · refine ⟨0, Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ (-n).toNat, ?_⟩
74	      rw [map_zero, zero_add, map_mul, Polynomial.aeval_C, map_pow, Polynomial.aeval_X,
75	        T_pow, ← C_eq_algebraMap]
76	      congr 2
77	      omega
78	
79	end LaurentPolynomial

83	variable {ι R A : Type*} [AddCommMonoid ι] [DecidableEq ι]
84	variable [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
85	variable (𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (x : Submonoid A)

87	lemma val_fromZeroRingHom (c : 𝒜 0) :
88	    (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x c).val = algebraMap A (Localization x) (c : A) := by
89	  have h : fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x c = HomogeneousLocalization.mk ⟨0, c, 1, one_mem x⟩ := rfl
90	  rw [h, val_mk, ← Localization.mk_one_eq_algebraMap]
91	  congr 1
92	
93	/-- If `A` is a graded `R`-algebra, then any homogeneous localization of `A` is an
94	`R`-algebra, via `R → 𝒜 0 → HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x`. The scalar action is the
95	existing pointwise one. -/
96	noncomputable instance : Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) where
97	  toSMul := inferInstanceAs (SMul R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x))
98	  algebraMap := (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0))
99	  commutes' _ _ := mul_comm _ _
100	  smul_def' r z := by
101	    apply val_injective
102	    change (r • z).val = ((fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0)) r * z).val
103	    rw [val_mul, val_smul x r z, RingHom.comp_apply, val_fromZeroRingHom,
104	      SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap]
105	    induction z.val using Localization.induction_on with
106	    | H w =>
107	      rw [Localization.smul_mk, ← Localization.mk_one_eq_algebraMap, Localization.mk_mul,
108	        Algebra.smul_def]
109	      exact congrArg (Localization.mk _) (Subtype.ext (one_mul _).symm)
110	
111	lemma algebraMap_eq' :
112	    algebraMap R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) =
113	      (fromZeroRingHom 𝒜 x).comp (algebraMap R (𝒜 0)) :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	instance : IsScalarTower R (𝒜 0) (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) :=
117	  .of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
118	
119	@[simp]
120	lemma algebraMap_val (r : R) :
121	    (algebraMap R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x) r).val =
122	      algebraMap A (Localization x) (algebraMap R A r) := by
123	  rw [algebraMap_eq', RingHom.comp_apply, val_fromZeroRingHom,
124	    SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap]
125	
126	end HomogeneousLocalization

134	/-- The projective line over `k`, as `Proj` of the standard graded ring `k[X₀, X₁]`. -/
135	noncomputable def P1 (k : Type u) [Field k] : Scheme.{u} :=
136	  Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
137	
138	namespace P1
139	
140	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
141	
142	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
143	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
144	
145	theorem fin_zero_ne_one : (0 : Fin 2) ≠ 1 := by decide
146	
147	theorem fin_one_ne_zero : (1 : Fin 2) ≠ 0 := by decide
148	
149	/-! ### The structure morphism and properness -/
150	
151	/-- The degree-zero part of `k[X₀,X₁]` is a trivial field extension of `k`. -/
152	noncomputable def gradeZeroAlgEquiv : k ≃ₐ[k] (𝒜 0) := by
153	  refine AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId k (𝒜 0)) ⟨fun a b hab => ?_, fun c => ?_⟩
154	  · have h : (MvPolynomial.C a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) = MvPolynomial.C b := by
155	      have h' := congrArg Subtype.val hab
156	      simpa [Algebra.ofId_apply, MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq] using h'
157	    exact MvPolynomial.C_injective _ _ h
158	  · have hc : (c : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ∈ (1 : Submodule k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) := by
159	      rw [← homogeneousSubmodule_zero (σ := Fin 2) (R := k)]
160	      exact c.2
161	    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Submodule.mem_one.mp hc
162	    exact ⟨r, Subtype.ext (by simpa [Algebra.ofId_apply] using hr)⟩
163	
164	instance : Algebra.FiniteType (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) :=
165	  have : IsScalarTower k (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) :=
166	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r => (SetLike.GradeZero.coe_algebraMap 𝒜 r).symm
167	  Algebra.FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType k (𝒜 0) (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
168	
169	/-- The structure morphism of the projective line over `k`. -/
170	noncomputable def structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
171	  Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))
172	
173	instance : IsIso (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) := by
174	  have : IsIso (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0))) :=
175	    (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr (gradeZeroAlgEquiv k).bijective
176	  infer_instance
177	
178	instance isProper_structureMap : IsProper (structureMap k) := by
179	  have h1 : IsProper (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜) := inferInstance
180	  have h2 : IsProper (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) := inferInstance
181	  exact IsProper.comp_iff.mpr h1
182	
183	/-- `P1 k` as an object over `Spec k`. -/
184	noncomputable def asOver : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (structureMap k)
185	
186	instance : IsProper (asOver k).hom :=
187	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (structureMap k))

189	/-! ### The standard affine charts -/
190	
191	/-- The variables of `k[X₀,X₁]` are homogeneous of degree one. -/
192	theorem X_mem (i : Fin 2) : X i ∈ 𝒜 1 :=
193	  X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k i
194	
195	/-- The product of the two variables is homogeneous of degree two. -/
196	theorem X_mul_X_mem : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 ∈ 𝒜 2 :=
197	  SetLike.mul_mem_graded (X_mem k 0) (X_mem k 1)
198	
199	/-- The chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` of the projective line. -/
200	noncomputable def chartOpen (i : Fin 2) : (P1 k).Opens :=
201	  Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)
202	
203	theorem isAffineOpen_chartOpen (i : Fin 2) : IsAffineOpen (chartOpen k i) :=
204	  Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
205	
206	theorem adjoin_gradeZero_range_X :
207	    Algebra.adjoin (𝒜 0) (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) = ⊤ := by
208	  rw [eq_top_iff]
209	  rintro p -
210	  have hp : p ∈ Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) := by
211	    rw [MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X]
212	    trivial
213	  induction hp using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
214	  | mem q hq => exact Algebra.subset_adjoin hq
215	  | algebraMap r =>
216	    exact Subalgebra.algebraMap_mem _
217	      (⟨algebraMap k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) r, by
218	        rw [MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq]
219	        exact (mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mpr (isHomogeneous_C _ r)⟩ : 𝒜 0)
220	  | add q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact add_mem h₁ h₂
221	  | mul q₁ q₂ _ _ h₁ h₂ => exact mul_mem h₁ h₂
222	
223	/-- The two standard charts cover the projective line. -/
224	theorem chartOpen_sup : chartOpen k 0 ⊔ chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
225	  have h := Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' 𝒜 (X : Fin 2 → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
226	    (fun i => ⟨1, X_mem k i⟩) (adjoin_gradeZero_range_X k)
227	  refine le_antisymm le_top (h.ge.trans (iSup_le fun i => ?_))
228	  fin_cases i
229	  · exact le_sup_left
230	  · exact le_sup_right
231	
232	/-- The overlap of the two standard charts is the basic open of `X₀X₁`. -/
233	theorem chartOpen_inf : chartOpen k 0 ⊓ chartOpen k 1 = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
234	  (Proj.basicOpen_mul 𝒜 (X 0) (X 1)).symm
235	
236	/-- The open immersion from the affine model `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀` onto the chart
237	`D₊(Xᵢ)` of the projective line. -/
238	noncomputable def chartι (i : Fin 2) :
239	    Spec (.of (Away 𝒜 (X i))) ⟶ P1 k :=
240	  Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
241	
242	instance (i : Fin 2) : IsOpenImmersion (chartι k i) :=
243	  inferInstanceAs (IsOpenImmersion (Proj.awayι _ _ _ _))
244	
245	theorem opensRange_chartι (i : Fin 2) : (chartι k i).opensRange = chartOpen k i :=
246	  Proj.opensRange_awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos
247	
248	/-- The chart inclusions are morphisms over `Spec k`. -/
249	theorem chartι_structureMap (i : Fin 2) :
250	    chartι k i ≫ structureMap k =
251	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)))) := by
252	  change Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos ≫
253	      (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) = _
254	  rw [Proj.awayι_toSpecZero_assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
255	
256	/-! ### The chart coordinate and the identification with the polynomial ring
257	
258	Throughout, `i j : Fin 2` are the two distinct indices; the chart coordinate on `D₊(Xᵢ)`
259	is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. -/
260	
261	/-- The chart coordinate `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ` in the section ring of the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)`. -/
262	noncomputable def chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) : Away 𝒜 (X i) :=
263	  Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j)
264	
265	theorem chartCoord_eq (i j : Fin 2) :
266	    chartCoord k i j = Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j) :=
267	  rfl
268	
269	theorem val_chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) :
270	    (chartCoord k i j).val = Localization.mk (X j)
271	      (⟨X i ^ 1, 1, rfl⟩ : Submonoid.powers (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)) :=
272	  rfl
273	
274	/-- Dehomogenization at `Xᵢ`: the `k`-algebra map `k[X₀,X₁] → k[t]` with `Xᵢ ↦ 1`,
275	`Xⱼ ↦ t`. -/
276	noncomputable def dehomogenize (i : Fin 2) :
277	    MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k →ₐ[k] Polynomial k :=
278	  MvPolynomial.aeval (Function.update (fun _ => Polynomial.X) i 1)
279	
280	@[simp]
281	theorem dehomogenize_X_self (i : Fin 2) : dehomogenize k i (X i) = 1 := by
282	  rw [dehomogenize, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, Function.update_self]
283	
284	theorem dehomogenize_X_of_ne {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
285	    dehomogenize k i (X j) = Polynomial.X := by
286	  rw [dehomogenize, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, Function.update_of_ne hij.symm]
287	
288	/-- `k[t] → (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`, `t ↦ Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. Bijective for `i ≠ j`; see `P1.awayAlgEquiv`. -/
289	noncomputable def polyToAway (i j : Fin 2) : Polynomial k →ₐ[k] Away 𝒜 (X i) :=
290	  Polynomial.aeval (chartCoord k i j)
291	
292	@[simp]
293	theorem polyToAway_X (i j : Fin 2) :
294	    polyToAway k i j Polynomial.X = chartCoord k i j :=
295	  Polynomial.aeval_X _
296	
297	theorem polyToAway_monomial (i j : Fin 2) (n : ℕ) (a : k) :
298	    polyToAway k i j (Polynomial.monomial n a) =
299	      algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) a * chartCoord k i j ^ n := by
300	  change Polynomial.aeval (chartCoord k i j) (Polynomial.monomial n a) = _
301	  exact Polynomial.aeval_monomial _
302	
303	theorem isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self (i : Fin 2) :
304	    IsUnit ((dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)) := by
305	  have h : (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i) = 1 := dehomogenize_X_self k i
306	  rw [h]
307	  exact isUnit_one
308	
309	/-- `(k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ → k[t]`, induced by dehomogenization at `Xᵢ`.
310	Inverse of `P1.polyToAway`; see `P1.awayAlgEquiv`. -/
311	noncomputable def awayToPoly (i : Fin 2) : Away 𝒜 (X i) →ₐ[k] Polynomial k where
312	  toRingHom :=
313	    (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)
314	      (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self k i)).comp
315	      (algebraMap (Away 𝒜 (X i)) (Localization.Away (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))
316	  commutes' r := by
317	    change (Localization.awayLift (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i)
318	        (isUnit_dehomogenize_X_self k i))
319	        ((algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) r).val) = algebraMap k (Polynomial k) r
320	    rw [HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_val, IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq]
321	    exact (dehomogenize k i).commutes r
322	
323	/-- The workhorse: `awayToPoly` sends `a/Xᵢⁿ` to the dehomogenization of `a`. -/
324	theorem awayToPoly_mk (i : Fin 2) (n : ℕ) (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)
325	    (ha : a ∈ 𝒜 (n • 1)) :
326	    awayToPoly k i (Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) n a ha) = dehomogenize k i a := by
327	  have h1 : (dehomogenize k i).toRingHom (X i) * 1 = 1 := by
328	    rw [mul_one]
329	    exact dehomogenize_X_self k i
330	  have h := Localization.awayLift_mk (A := Polynomial k)
331	    ((dehomogenize k i).toRingHom) (X i) a 1 h1 n
332	  exact h.trans (by rw [one_pow, mul_one]; rfl)
333	
334	@[simp]
335	theorem awayToPoly_chartCoord {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
336	    awayToPoly k i (chartCoord k i j) = Polynomial.X :=
337	  (awayToPoly_mk k i 1 (X j) (by simpa using X_mem k j)).trans (dehomogenize_X_of_ne k hij)
338	
339	theorem awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
340	    (awayToPoly k i).comp (polyToAway k i j) = AlgHom.id k (Polynomial k) := by
341	  apply Polynomial.algHom_ext
342	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, polyToAway_X, awayToPoly_chartCoord k hij, AlgHom.id_apply]
343	
344	theorem awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (p : Polynomial k) :
345	    awayToPoly k i (polyToAway k i j p) = p :=
346	  AlgHom.congr_fun (awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway k hij) p
347	
348	section Surjectivity
349	
350	theorem prod_X_pow_eq {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (e : Fin 2 → ℕ) :
351	    (∏ l, (X l : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ^ e l) = X i ^ e i * X j ^ e j := by
352	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [Fin.prod_univ_two, mul_comm]
353	
354	theorem sum_fin_two_eq {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (e : Fin 2 → ℕ) :
355	    e i + e j = e 0 + e 1 := by
356	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [add_comm]
357	
358	theorem chartCoord_pow (i j : Fin 2) (m : ℕ) :
359	    chartCoord k i j ^ m =
360	      Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) m (X j ^ m)
361	        (by simpa using SetLike.pow_mem_graded m (X_mem k j)) := by
362	  rw [ext_iff_val, val_pow, val_chartCoord, Away.val_mk, Localization.mk_pow,
363	    Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff, Localization.r_iff_exists]
364	  exact ⟨1, by push_cast; ring⟩
365	
366	theorem away_mk_prod_eq {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) (a : ℕ) (e : Fin 2 → ℕ)
367	    (hae : e 0 + e 1 = a)
368	    (H : (∏ l, (X l : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) ^ e l) ∈ 𝒜 (a • 1)) :
369	    Away.mk 𝒜 (X_mem k i) a (∏ l, X l ^ e l) H = chartCoord k i j ^ e j := by
370	  have hij' : e i + e j = a := (sum_fin_two_eq hij e).trans hae
371	  rw [chartCoord_pow, ext_iff_val, Away.val_mk, Away.val_mk, Localization.mk_eq_mk_iff,
372	    Localization.r_iff_exists]
373	  refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
374	  push_cast
375	  rw [prod_X_pow_eq k hij e, ← hij']
376	  ring
377	
378	theorem polyToAway_surjective {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
379	    Function.Surjective (polyToAway k i j) := by
380	  intro z
381	  have hz : z ∈ (⊤ : Submodule (𝒜 0) (Away 𝒜 (X i))) := trivial
382	  rw [← Away.span_mk_prod_pow_eq_top (X_mem k i) X (adjoin_gradeZero_range_X k)
383	    (fun _ => 1) (fun l => X_mem k l)] at hz
384	  induction hz using Submodule.span_induction with
385	  | mem w hw =>
386	    obtain ⟨a, e, hae, rfl⟩ := hw
387	    refine ⟨Polynomial.X ^ e j, ?_⟩
388	    rw [map_pow, polyToAway_X]
389	    exact (away_mk_prod_eq k hij a e (by simpa using hae) _).symm
390	  | zero => exact ⟨0, map_zero _⟩
391	  | add u v _ _ hu hv =>
392	    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hu
393	    obtain ⟨q, rfl⟩ := hv
394	    exact ⟨p + q, map_add _ _ _⟩
395	  | smul c w _ hw =>
396	    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := hw
397	    obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := (gradeZeroAlgEquiv k).surjective c
398	    refine ⟨r • p, ?_⟩
399	    rw [map_smul]
400	    change r • polyToAway k i j p = (algebraMap k (𝒜 0) r) • polyToAway k i j p
401	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, smul_assoc, one_smul]
402	
403	end Surjectivity

405	theorem polyToAway_comp_awayToPoly {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
406	    (polyToAway k i j).comp (awayToPoly k i) = AlgHom.id k (Away 𝒜 (X i)) := by
407	  refine AlgHom.ext fun z => ?_
408	  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := polyToAway_surjective k hij z
409	  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.id_apply, awayToPoly_polyToAway_apply k hij]
410	
411	/-- The chart identification: the section ring `(k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀` of the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` is a
412	polynomial ring over `k`, with variable the chart coordinate `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`. -/
413	noncomputable def awayAlgEquiv {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
414	    Away 𝒜 (X i) ≃ₐ[k] Polynomial k :=
415	  AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom (awayToPoly k i) (polyToAway k i j)
416	    (awayToPoly_comp_polyToAway k hij) (polyToAway_comp_awayToPoly k hij)
417	
418	@[simp]
419	theorem awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
420	    awayAlgEquiv k hij (chartCoord k i j) = Polynomial.X :=
421	  awayToPoly_chartCoord k hij
422	
423	@[simp]
424	theorem awayAlgEquiv_symm_X {i j : Fin 2} (hij : i ≠ j) :
425	    (awayAlgEquiv k hij).symm Polynomial.X = chartCoord k i j :=

254	/-- **The chart-ring span core.**  The degree-zero away ring `(ℤ[X₀,X₁]_{X₀})₀`
255	is spanned, over its constant subring `𝒜 0`, by the powers of the coordinate
256	fraction `X₁/X₀ = p1CoordAway ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩`: every degree-zero away element is a
257	`(𝒜 0)`-linear combination of `(X₁/X₀)^m`.  This is the mathematical heart of the
258	chart-ring spanning `Γ(V₀) = k[x]`.
259	
260	The proof: every away element is `p / X₀^N` with `p` homogeneous of degree `N`
261	(`Away.mk_surjective`); expanding `p` over its monomial support and using that
262	each occurring exponent vector `d` satisfies `d₀ + d₁ = N` (homogeneity), the
263	per-monomial identity `awayMk_monomial_mem_span` writes each summand as a
264	constant times a coordinate power, so the whole fraction lands in the span. -/
265	theorem span_p1CoordAway_pow_top :
266	    (⊤ : Submodule (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)
267	        (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩)))
268	      ≤ Submodule.span (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)
269	          (Set.range fun m : ℕ => p1CoordAway (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩ ^ m) := by
270	  intro w _
271	  obtain ⟨N, a, ha, rfl⟩ := HomogeneousLocalization.Away.mk_surjective
272	    (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
273	    (ProjTwist.X_mem_deg_one (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩) w
274	  have hhom := (mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mp ha
275	  -- each monomial summand of `a` is homogeneous of degree `N • 1`
276	  have hmonoAll : ∀ d : ULift.{u} (Fin 2) →₀ ℕ,
277	      (monomial d (coeff d a) : MvPolynomial (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ∈
278	        homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) (N • 1) := by
279	    intro d
280	    rcases eq_or_ne (coeff d a) 0 with h0 | h0
281	    · rw [h0, monomial_zero]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
282	    · refine (mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mpr (isHomogeneous_monomial _ ?_)
283	      by_contra hne
284	      exact h0 (hhom.coeff_eq_zero hne)
285	  -- every support exponent `d` has total degree `d₀ + d₁ = N`
286	  have hdegN : ∀ d ∈ a.support, d ⟨0⟩ + d ⟨1⟩ = N := by
287	    intro d hd
288	    rw [mem_support_iff] at hd
289	    have hdeg : Finsupp.degree d = N • 1 := by
290	      by_contra hne
291	      exact hd (hhom.coeff_eq_zero hne)
292	    rw [Finsupp.degree_eq_sum,
293	        ← Equiv.sum_comp (Equiv.ulift.symm : Fin 2 ≃ ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (fun i => d i),
294	        Fin.sum_univ_two] at hdeg

297	  have hsum : Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
298	        (ProjTwist.X_mem_deg_one (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩) N a ha
299	      = ∑ d ∈ a.support, Away.mk (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
300	          (ProjTwist.X_mem_deg_one (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩) N (monomial d (coeff d a))
301	          (hmonoAll d) := by
302	    apply HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective
303	    rw [Away.val_mk, ← HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply, map_sum]
304	    simp only [HomogeneousLocalization.algebraMap_apply, Away.val_mk]
305	    rw [← Localization.mk_sum, ← MvPolynomial.as_sum]
306	  rw [hsum]
307	  refine Submodule.sum_mem _ (fun d hd => ?_)
308	  exact awayMk_monomial_mem_span N d (coeff d a) (hdegN d hd) (hmonoAll d)

351	  exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨d ⟨0⟩, rfl⟩)

400	/-! ## Transporting the span core through a ring hom (route step 2, algebraic heart)
401	
402	The char-free "push the `ℤ`-span through `k ⊗_ℤ (−)`".  For **any** ring hom `ρ`
403	from the degree-zero away ring `(ℤ[X₀,X₁]_{X₀})₀` into a `k`-algebra `B`, the image
404	`ρ a` of every away element lies in the `k`-span of the powers of `ρ (X₁/X₀)`.  The
405	`(𝒜 0) = ℤ`-scalars of the span core (`span_p1CoordAway_pow_top`) become `k`-scalars
406	because a ring hom sends integer constants of `𝒜 0` to integers of `B`, which are
407	`k`-multiples of `1`.  Applied to the pullback ring map `Away 𝒜 X₀ → Γ(V₀)` (whose
408	value at `X₁/X₀` is the chart coordinate `x`), this is exactly the transport of the
409	span through the tensor identification `Γ(V₀) = k ⊗_ℤ (ℤ[X₁/X₀])`. -/
410	
411	section SpanTransport
412	
413	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
414	
415	/-- Every element of the degree-zero part `𝒜 0` (the copy of `ℤ` given by the
416	constants) is an integer constant. -/
417	private lemma exists_intCast_eq_gradeZero
418	    (c : (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)) :
419	    ∃ m : ℤ, (m : (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)) = c := by
420	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ :=
421	    (ProjectiveSpace.bijective_algebraMap_gradeZero (ULift.{u} (Fin 2))).surjective c
422	  refine ⟨z.down, ?_⟩
423	  rw [← hz, ← map_intCast (algebraMap (ULift.{u} ℤ)
424	    (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)) z.down]
425	  rfl
426	
427	/-- **Route step 2, algebraic core: transport of the span through a ring hom.**
428	For any ring hom `ρ` from the degree-zero away ring `(ℤ[X₀,X₁]_{X₀})₀` into a
429	`k`-algebra `B`, the image `ρ a` of every away element lies in the `k`-span of the
430	powers of `ρ (X₁/X₀)`. -/
431	lemma awayRingHom_mem_span_pow {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
432	    (ρ : Away (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩) →+* B)
433	    (a : Away (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩)) :
434	    ρ a ∈ Submodule.span k
435	      (Set.range fun m : ℕ => ρ (p1CoordAway (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩) ^ m) := by
436	  have hmem : a ∈ Submodule.span (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)
437	      (Set.range fun m : ℕ => p1CoordAway (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩ ^ m) :=
438	    span_p1CoordAway_pow_top (Submodule.mem_top)
439	  induction hmem using Submodule.span_induction with
440	  | mem z hz =>
441	      obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := hz
442	      exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, by rw [map_pow]⟩
443	  | zero => rw [map_zero]; exact Submodule.zero_mem _
444	  | add u v _ _ hu hv => rw [map_add]; exact Submodule.add_mem _ hu hv
445	  | smul c u _ hu =>
446	      obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := exists_intCast_eq_gradeZero c
447	      rw [Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul, map_zsmul, ← Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul k]
448	      exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ hu
449	
450	end SpanTransport

452	/-! ## Base change spans (route step 2, general algebra) -/
453	
454	section BaseChangeSpan
455	
456	/-- **Base change is spanned by the image.**  If `N` is the base change of the
457	`R`-module `M` to `S` (`IsBaseChange S f` for `f : M →ₗ[R] N`), then `N` is
458	spanned over `S` by the image of `f` — because `N ≃ S ⊗[R] M` and every pure
459	tensor `s ⊗ m = s • f m` lies in the `S`-span of the range. -/
460	theorem isBaseChange_span_range_eq_top {R S M N : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
461	    [CommSemiring S] [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R M] [Module R N]
462	    [Algebra R S] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] {f : M →ₗ[R] N}
463	    (hf : IsBaseChange S f) :
464	    Submodule.span S (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by
465	  rw [eq_top_iff]
466	  rintro n -
467	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := hf.equiv.surjective n
468	  refine TensorProduct.induction_on t (by simp) (fun s m => ?_)
469	    (fun x y hx hy => by rw [map_add]; exact Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy)
470	  rw [hf.equiv_tmul]
471	  exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, rfl⟩)
472	
473	open scoped Pointwise in
474	/-- The `k`-span of the powers of a single element `x` is closed under
475	multiplication (`xᵃ · xᵇ = xᵃ⁺ᵇ` is again a power), hence a subring — the fact
476	that makes it the target of a `Subring.closure` induction. -/
477	theorem mul_mem_span_range_pow {k A : Type*} [CommRing k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
478	    (x : A) {a b : A}
479	    (ha : a ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n))
480	    (hb : b ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n)) :
481	    a * b ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n) := by
482	  have hSS : (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n) * (Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n)
483	      ⊆ Set.range fun n : ℕ => x ^ n := by
484	    rw [Set.mul_subset_iff]
485	    rintro _ ⟨p, rfl⟩ _ ⟨q, rfl⟩
486	    exact ⟨p + q, by simp only [pow_add]⟩
487	  have hmul := Submodule.mul_mem_mul ha hb
488	  rw [Submodule.span_mul_span] at hmul
489	  exact Submodule.span_mono hSS hmul
490	
491	end BaseChangeSpan

493	section BaseChange

495	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
496	
497	open ProjectiveSpace HomogeneousLocalization
498	
499	/-- The `algebraSection` `k`-module structure on `Γ(V₀)` (registered locally so
500	the span statement uses the same module structure as `LaurentChartData.span_pow_x`
501	will at the assembly site). -/
502	noncomputable local instance instAlgebraΓV0 :
503	    Algebra k Γ(ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), p1Chart k ⟨0⟩) :=
504	  Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.algebraSection
505	    (Over.mk (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

508	/-- The affine-chart map `awayToSection : (ℤ[X]_{X₀})₀ → Γ(D₊(X₀))` is surjective:
509	it is the isomorphism `basicOpenIsoAway` (`X₀` is homogeneous of degree `1 > 0`). -/
510	private lemma awayToSection_X0_surjective :
511	    Function.Surjective ⇑(Proj.awayToSection
512	      (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩)) := by
513	  haveI : IsIso (Proj.awayToSection
514	      (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩)) := by
515	    rw [← Proj.basicOpenIsoAway_hom (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
516	      (X ⟨0⟩) (ProjTwist.X_mem_deg_one (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) ⟨0⟩) one_pos]

520	/-- **`V₀`-generators of type (1): the `Proj`-side.**  The `toProjInt`-pullback of a
521	section `s ∈ Γ(D₊(X₀))` lies in the `k`-span of the powers of `x = p1XSection`.
522	Writing `s = awayToSection a` (the affine chart iso, `awayToSection_X0_surjective`)
523	and reducing `appLE` to `app` (the chart open is `toProjInt ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(X₀)`), the pullback
524	is `ρ a` for the ring hom `ρ = appLE ∘ awayToSection`; every `a` is a `(𝒜 0)`-combination
525	of the coordinate powers (`span_p1CoordAway_pow_top`), and `ρ` carries those to the powers
526	of `x`, the `(𝒜 0) = ℤ`-scalars becoming `k`-scalars (`exists_intCast_eq_gradeZero`). -/
527	private lemma mem_span_appLE_toProjInt
528	    (s : Γ(Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)),
529	        Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩))) :
530	    (Scheme.Hom.appLE (toProjInt (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
531	        (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩))
532	        (p1Chart k ⟨0⟩) (le_refl _)).hom s
533	      ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun n : ℕ => p1XSection k ^ n) := by
534	  have hbridge : Scheme.Hom.appLE (toProjInt (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
535	        (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩))
536	        (p1Chart k ⟨0⟩) (le_refl _)
537	      = (toProjInt (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))).app
538	          (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ)) (X ⟨0⟩)) :=
539	    Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
540	  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := awayToSection_X0_surjective s
541	  -- `ρ = appLE ∘ awayToSection`, with an *explicit source type* (`let` for transparency)
542	  let ρ : Away (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ULift.{u} ℤ))
543	        (X (⟨0⟩ : ULift.{u} (Fin 2))) →+*
544	      Γ(ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), p1Chart k ⟨0⟩) :=
545	    (Scheme.Hom.appLE (toProjInt (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.P1SectionsFinite
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StructureSheafPushforward

/-!
# B3-H0, the last anchor: `Γ(ℙ¹_A, 𝒪) = A` reduced to a single statement over `k`

`Picard/P1SectionsFinite.lean` reduced the Serre-finiteness-grade hypothesis
`hH0` of the B3 ℙ¹ engine (finite generation of the Čech `H⁰ = Γ(ℙ¹_A, M)`
for a finitely presented `M`) to one `M`-independent *structure-sheaf* anchor:
bijectivity of the comparison map

`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) ⟶ Γ(ℙ¹_A, 𝒪)`  (`p1Cech_h0_fg_of_bijective_appTop`, :1298)

— but left it quantified over every finitely generated `k`-algebra `A`.  This
file removes the `A` from the anchor.  What remains is the single, classical,
`A`-free statement

**`Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k`** (`Function.Bijective ((p1Over k).hom.appTop).hom`),

equivalently — via the unconditional field-of-constants machinery of
`Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean` — the mathlib class
`GeometricallyIntegral (p1Over k).hom`.

## Why the `A` disappears

The `B1` brick `bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange`
(`Picard/StructureSheafPushforward.lean`:80) already does exactly this
reduction, but it is stated for a proper *geometrically integral* `C/k`, so it
cannot be applied to `ℙ¹` before geometric integrality of `ℙ¹` is available.
Reading its proof shows that geometric integrality is used **only** to obtain
`Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` (`bijective_hom_appTop`); every other ingredient — the qcqs `H⁰`
flat base change `globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv` — needs nothing beyond
`CompactSpace`/`QuasiSeparatedSpace` on the total space, because the base
`Spec k` is a field, hence every `Spec A ⟶ Spec k` is flat.  §1 therefore
restates the brick with the field-of-constants conclusion taken as a
*hypothesis*:

`bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange_of_bijective_appTop` — for **any** qcqs
`k`-scheme `X` with `Γ(X, 𝒪) = k`, the comparison `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(X_A, 𝒪)`
is bijective for **every** `k`-algebra `A`.

`ℙ¹_k` is proper (`ProjectiveSpace.isProper_over`), hence qcqs (§2), so §3
turns the single anchor into the engine's `hH0` at every `A`, and §4 records
the engine conclusion in that form.

## The remaining frontier of this file

`Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k` is *not* proved here.  It is the standard fact that the
projective line over a field has no nonconstant global regular functions; in
this tree the route to it is `GeometricallyIntegral` of the structural
morphism of relative projective space, which by `MorphismProperty.pullback_fst`
reduces (§3b) to geometric integrality of the integral model
`Proj ℤ[X₀, X₁] ⟶ ⊤_Scheme`, i.e. to `IsIntegral (ℙ¹_K)` for *every* field
`K` — a genuinely missing mathlib result about `Proj`, not a gap in the B3
argument.

**§5 sharpens this considerably.**  The `hH0` leaf does not actually need
`Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k`: the Serre-dévissage anchor
`fg_ker_ringSectionDiffBase_of_module_finite_top` consumes only *finiteness*
of `Γ(ℙ¹_A, 𝒪)` over `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪)`, and over a field base finiteness
base-changes along the same `H⁰` flat base change.  Over `k`, finiteness for a
proper scheme is mathlib's `finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`, whose only
non-properness hypothesis is `IsIntegral X`.  So the sharpest form of the
frontier is

**`IsIntegral (ℙ¹_k)`** (`p1Cech_h0_fg_of_isIntegral`),

a statement about the *one* field `k`.  It is strictly weaker than geometric
integrality (`isIntegral_p1Over_left_of_geometricallyIntegral`).  It is **not**
comparable with `Γ(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = k`: neither implies the other (a double line in
`ℙ²` has `Γ(X, 𝒪) = k` and is not reduced, so `P1HasTrivialConstants` does not
force integrality; and integrality does not by itself force the field of
constants to be `k`).  Both anchors are kept because each independently
discharges `hH0`: §3–§4 for the sharp field-of-constants statement (which other
campaign consumers want in its own right), §5 for the one that needs less.

Sources: Mumford AV II §5; Stacks 01XZ/01YS; EGA III 3.2.1 (the classical
`H⁰`-finiteness this file replaces by an elementary anchor); Kleiman,
*The Picard scheme*, §5.
-/

/-! ## §1. `H⁰` base change over a field base, with the field of constants as a hypothesis

The `B1` brick with `[GeometricallyIntegral]` traded for the only consequence
of it the proof uses. -/

open TensorProduct in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- **`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) ≅ Γ(X ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` from `Γ(X, 𝒪) = k`.**  For a qcqs
`k`-scheme `X` (e.g. proper) whose structure map `k → Γ(X, 𝒪)` is *bijective*
— the field-of-constants conclusion, taken here as a hypothesis rather than
derived from geometric integrality — the comparison map
`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(X ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is bijective for **every** `k`-algebra
`A`.

This is `Picard/StructureSheafPushforward.lean`'s `bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange`
with its `[IsProper] [GeometricallyIntegral]` hypotheses weakened to exactly
what its proof consumes: the qcqs `H⁰` flat base change
`globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv` (unconditional over a field base, since
`Spec A ⟶ Spec k` is automatically flat) composed with `includeLeft`, which
is bijective precisely because the right tensor factor `Γ(X, 𝒪)` collapses to
`k`. -/
theorem bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange_of_bijective_appTop
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (iX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hX : Function.Bijective (iX.appTop).hom)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
    Function.Bijective
      ((pullback.snd iX
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).appTop).hom := by
  set g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) with hg
  letI instSA : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) :=
    ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
  letI instMA : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(X, ⊤) :=
    (iX.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
  letI instPull : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
      ↥Γ(pullback iX g, ⊤) :=
    ((pullback.snd iX g).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
  have e := globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv iX A
  set R := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
  set S := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
  set M := ↥Γ(X, ⊤)
  have hRM : Function.Bijective (algebraMap R M) := hX
  let φ : M ≃ₐ[R] R := (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId R M) hRM).symm
  let ε : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₐ[S] S :=
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr AlgEquiv.refl φ).trans (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid R S S)
  have hb2 : ∀ s : S, algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M) s = ε.symm s := by
    intro s
    have h := ε.commutes s
    simp only [Algebra.algebraMap_self, RingHom.id_apply] at h
    exact ε.eq_symm_apply.mpr h
  have hleft : Function.Bijective ⇑(algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M)) := by
    have : ⇑(algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M)) = ⇑ε.symm := funext hb2
    rw [this]; exact ε.symm.bijective
  change Function.Bijective ⇑(algebraMap S ↥Γ(pullback iX g, ⊤))
  have hcomp : ⇑(algebraMap S ↥Γ(pullback iX g, ⊤))
      = ⇑e ∘ ⇑(algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M)) := by
    funext s; exact (e.commutes s).symm
  rw [hcomp]
  exact e.bijective.comp hleft

end Scheme

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-! ## §2. `ℙ¹_k` is proper, hence qcqs

`Adelic.p1Over k` is `Over.mk` of the structural morphism of relative
projective space, so the `ProjectiveSpace` instances have to be transported
through `Over.mk` by hand (typeclass search does not unfold `Over.mk`). -/

/-- `ℙ¹_k ⟶ Spec k` is proper (`ProjectiveSpace.isProper_over`, transported
through `Over.mk`). -/
instance isProper_p1Over_hom : IsProper ((p1Over k).hom) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ↘
    Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

/-- `ℙ¹_k` is quasi-compact (proper ⟹ quasi-compact over the quasi-compact

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, hold a 1-to-1 correspondence with the Lean, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. Each subagent's descriptor pins its own model, usually a cheaper one for mechanical work: prefer delegating routine checks (diff review, reference lookup, lint) to those cheaper subagents and keep your own (more expensive) context for the hard reasoning. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

11	/-!
12	# Serre finiteness for the section graded module (statement)
13	
14	The deep remaining input of the Hilbert-polynomial lane
15	(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`, inbox `I-0109`): for a projective scheme over
16	a field carrying a very ample line bundle `L` and a coherent sheaf `F`, the
17	section graded ring `R(X, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, L^{⊗m})` is Noetherian, the section
18	graded module `M(X, F, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite module over it,
19	and each graded component is a finite-dimensional `κ`-vector space.

21	This file gives the **honest statement** against the projectivity vocabulary
22	of `Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean` (the `IsProjectiveWith` closed-immersion
23	predicate — very ampleness in the encoding settled in inbox `I-0118`), as a
24	named typed `sorry` leaf: the proof is Serre's theorem ([Hartshorne] II.5.17
25	ff., [Nitsure] §1) and is genuinely deep (multi-session; it needs the
26	pushforward-to-projective-space reduction and cohomological finiteness on

30	passes to a Veronese power, the Lean statement hypothesises the very ample
31	form directly (`IsProjectiveWith`) — this is the form in which the

46	/-- The structural `κ`-algebra structure on the global sections of a scheme
47	over `Spec κ` (the absolute analogue of `Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`). -/
48	def Scheme.Hom.structuralSectionsHom {X : Scheme.{0}} {κ : Type} [CommRing κ]
49	    (π : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) : κ →+* Γ(X, ⊤) :=
50	  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of κ)).inv ≫ π.appTop).hom

52	/-- **Serre finiteness for the section graded module**
53	(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`; [Nitsure] §1, [Hartshorne] II.5.17 ff.):
54	for `π : X ⟶ Spec κ` projective carrying the very ample line bundle `L`
55	and a coherent (finitely presented) sheaf `F` on `X`,
56	
57	1. the section graded ring `⊕ₘ Γ(X, L^{⊗m})` is Noetherian;
58	2. the section graded module `⊕ₘ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite module

65	cohomological finiteness of coherent sheaves on projective space. -/
66	theorem sectionGradedModule_fg {X : Scheme.{0}} {κ : Type} [Field κ]
67	    (π : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) (L F : X.Modules)
68	    (hproj : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) :
69	    (letI := Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedRing_gsemiring L
70	     IsNoetherianRing (DirectSum ℕ (Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg L)))
71	    ∧ (letI := Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedRing_gsemiring L
72	       letI := Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedModule_gmodule F L
73	       Module.Finite (DirectSum ℕ (Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg L))
74	         (DirectSum ℕ (Scheme.Modules.moduleSectionDeg F L)))
75	    ∧ ∀ m : ℕ,

87	a field.  The lemmas below are the sorry-free geometric glue that transports
88	`IsProjectiveWith` and finite presentation to a fibre (both via the already
89	proved `IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` and `Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation`),
90	so the deep Serre leaf applies fibrewise; the corollary

97	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}}

99	/-- **`IsProjectiveWith` descends to scheme-theoretic fibres**: if `π : X ⟶ S`
100	is projective carrying `L`, then the structural morphism of the fibre
101	`X_s = π.fiber s`, namely `π.fiberToSpecResidueField s : X_s ⟶ Spec κ(s)`, is
102	projective carrying the restriction `L_s = π.fiberModule s L`.  Immediate from
103	`IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` along `S.fromSpecResidueField s`, since the fibre
104	is the base change of `π` along that morphism (`Scheme.Hom.fiber`). -/
105	theorem Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.fiber {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
106	    (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (s : S) :
107	    (π.fiberToSpecResidueField s).IsProjectiveWith (π.fiberModule s L) :=
108	  h.baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)

110	/-- **Finite presentation descends to scheme-theoretic fibres**: the restriction
111	`F_s = π.fiberModule s F` of a finitely presented sheaf `F` to the fibre is

114	theorem Scheme.Hom.fiberModule_isFinitePresentation (π : X ⟶ S) (s : S)
115	    {F : X.Modules} (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) :
116	    (π.fiberModule s F).IsFinitePresentation :=

165	/-! ## Engine-ready packaging and the rationality of the Hilbert function
166	
167	The graded Hilbert–Serre rationality engine
168	`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedModule_hilbertSeries_rational`
169	(`Picard/GradedHilbertSerre.lean`, sorry-free) turns an abstract finitely
170	generated `ℕ`-graded `κ`-vector space — one carrying `r` commuting degree-one
171	endomorphisms and finite over the polynomial ring `κ[X₀,…,X_{r-1}]` — into a
172	rational Hilbert function (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsRatHilb`).  To feed the geometric
173	fibre section module `⊕ₘ Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` into that engine we package its

183	
184	/-- **Engine-ready packaging of Serre finiteness** for a Hilbert function
185	`f : ℕ → ℕ` over a field `κ`: a finitely generated (over a polynomial ring in `r`
186	degree-one variables) `ℕ`-graded `κ`-vector space whose `n`-th graded piece has
187	dimension `f n`.  This bundles exactly the data and hypotheses consumed by the
188	graded Hilbert–Serre rationality engine
189	`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedModule_hilbertSeries_rational`; the engine call is
190	`GradedHilbert.isRatHilb`.  Geometrically `M` is the fibre section module
191	`⊕ₘ Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})`, `grading n` is its `n`-th piece, and `gen` are the
192	`d+1` multiplications by the homogeneous coordinate sections. -/
193	structure GradedHilbert (κ : Type u) [Field κ] (f : ℕ → ℕ) where
194	  /-- Number of degree-one polynomial generators (`d+1` homogeneous coordinates). -/
195	  r : ℕ
196	  /-- The ambient graded `κ`-vector space. -/
197	  M : Type u
198	  [addCommGroup : AddCommGroup M]
199	  [module : Module κ M]
200	  /-- The internal `ℕ`-grading. -/
201	  grading : ℕ → Submodule κ M
202	  [decomposition : DirectSum.Decomposition grading]
203	  /-- Each graded piece is finite-dimensional. -/
204	  finiteDimensional : ∀ n, FiniteDimensional κ (grading n)
205	  /-- The `r` commuting degree-one endomorphisms (coordinate multiplications). -/
206	  gen : Fin r → Module.End κ M
207	  /-- The generators commute. -/
208	  gen_comm : ∀ i j, Commute (gen i) (gen j)
209	  /-- Each generator raises the grading degree by one. -/
210	  gen_raisesDegree : ∀ i, GradedModule.RaisesDegree grading (gen i)
211	  /-- The graded pieces realise the prescribed dimensions `f`. -/
212	  finrank_grading : ∀ n, Module.finrank κ (grading n) = f n
213	  /-- `M` is finite over the polynomial ring `κ[X₀,…,X_{r-1}]` acting via `gen`. -/
214	  finite : letI := GradedModule.polyModule gen gen_comm
215	    Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin r) κ) M

217	-- Register the carried instances as the *projection* instances of the structure, so
218	-- typeclass search returns exactly the terms appearing in `GradedHilbert.finite`'s type

220	attribute [instance] GradedHilbert.addCommGroup GradedHilbert.module
221	  GradedHilbert.decomposition GradedHilbert.finiteDimensional

223	/-- The Hilbert function packaged by a `GradedHilbert` datum is a rational Hilbert

227	theorem GradedHilbert.isRatHilb {κ : Type u} [Field κ] {f : ℕ → ℕ}

232	  have h : IsRatHilb (fun n => (Module.finrank κ (H.grading n) : ℚ)) H.r :=

234	      H.gen_raisesDegree H.finite

236	      = fun n => (Module.finrank κ (H.grading n) : ℚ) := by
237	    funext n; rw [H.finrank_grading]
238	  rw [hfun]; exact h

259	theorem gradedHilbert_fiber (π : X ⟶ S) (L F : X.Modules) (s : S)

10	/-!
11	# Projective morphisms carrying a very ample line bundle
12	
13	Mathlib v4.31 has no projective-morphism class and no (very) ampleness
14	vocabulary.  Following the encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment
15	`C-0002`), this file defines:
16	
17	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n₀ S m` — the Serre twist `O(m)` on the
18	  relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`, the pullback of
19	  `ProjTwist.serreTwist` from the integral model along `toProjInt`;
20	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheafBaseChange` — `O(m)` commutes with base
21	  change of the ambient projective space;
22	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith π L` — the **projective-with-`L`** predicate:
23	  `π : X ⟶ S` factors through a closed immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(Fin (d+1); S)`
24	  over `S` with `L ≅ i^* O(1)`;
25	
26	with the stability facts the Quot-scheme endgame consumes:
27	
28	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.isProper` — projective morphisms are proper;
29	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.comp_isClosedImmersion` — a closed immersion
30	  into a projective scheme is projective (carrying the restricted bundle);
31	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` — stability under base change
32	  (carrying the pulled-back bundle).
33	
34	Everything is at `Scheme.{0}`: the Serre twist rests on the descent engine
35	`Scheme.Modules.glue`, which is universe-monomorphic at `Scheme.GlueData.{0}`
36	(`GlueDescent.lean:934`).

54	/-- The Serre twist `O(m)` on the relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`:
55	the pullback of the glued twisting sheaf on the integral model. -/
56	def twistingSheaf (m : ℕ) : (ℙ(n₀; S)).Modules :=
57	  (Scheme.Modules.pullback (toProjInt n₀ S)).obj (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)

66	  Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (map_toProjInt n₀ g) (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)

73	pullback of the Serre twist `O(1)`.  This is the faithful encoding of
74	"projective with relatively very ample `L`" settled in inbox `I-0118`. -/

79	      Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj

90	  obtain ⟨d, i, hi, hcomp, -⟩ := h
91	  haveI := hi
92	  rw [← hcomp]

152	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheafBaseChange (Fin (d + 1)) g 1)
153	
154	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith

8	/-!
9	# Relative projective space `ℙ(n; S)`
10	
11	Mathlib v4.31 has the absolute `Proj` of a ℕ-graded ring together with the
12	properness package for `Proj.toSpecZero` (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`),
13	but no relative projective space over an arbitrary base scheme.  Following the
14	`AffineSpace` pattern (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean`) and the
15	encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment `C-0002`), this file defines
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n S` (notation `ℙ(n; S)`): the relative
18	  projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by `n : Type u`, i.e.
19	  the pullback of the integral model
20	  `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n] = Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ))`
21	  along `S ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme`;
22	* the structural morphism `ℙ(n; S) ↘ S` (a `CanonicallyOver` instance) with
23	  `IsProper` (hence `IsSeparated`, `UniversallyClosed`, `LocallyOfFiniteType`,
24	  `QuasiCompact`) derived by base change from the Mathlib instances on
25	  `Proj.toSpecZero`;

27	  `ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map`.
28

/-- We say that morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is geometrically integral if for all `Spec K ⟶ Y` with `K`
a field, `X ×[Y] Spec K` is integral. -/
@[mk_iff]
class GeometricallyIntegral (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop where
  geometrically_isIntegral : geometrically IsIntegral f

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometrically :
    @GeometricallyIntegral = geometrically IsIntegral := by
  ext; exact geometricallyIntegral_iff _

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible :
    @GeometricallyIntegral =
      (@GeometricallyReduced ⊓ @GeometricallyIrreducible : MorphismProperty Scheme) := by
  rw [eq_geometrically, GeometricallyReduced.eq_geometrically,
    GeometricallyIrreducible.eq_geometrically, ← geometrically_inf]
  eta_expand
  simp [isIntegral_iff_irreducibleSpace_and_isReduced, and_comm]

instance (priority := low) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyReduced f :=
  (GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible.le _ _ _ ‹_›).1

instance (priority := low) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyIrreducible f :=
  (GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible.le _ _ _ ‹_›).2

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [GeometricallyIrreducible f] :
    GeometricallyIntegral f :=
  GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible.ge _ _ _ ⟨‹_›, ‹_›⟩

instance : IsStableUnderBaseChange @GeometricallyIntegral :=
  GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometrically ▸ inferInstance

instance [GeometricallyIntegral g] : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.fst f g) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_fst f g inferInstance

instance [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.snd f g) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd f g inferInstance

instance (V : S.Opens) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyIntegral (f ∣_ V) :=
  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (isPullback_morphismRestrict ..).flip ‹_›

instance (s : S) [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
    GeometricallyIntegral (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance

instance (s : S) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : IsIntegral (f.fiber s) :=
  GeometricallyIntegral.geometrically_isIntegral _ _ _ (.of_hasPullback _ _)

13	/-!
14	# Relative projective space `ℙ(n; S)`
15	
16	Mathlib v4.31 has the absolute `Proj` of a ℕ-graded ring together with the
17	properness package for `Proj.toSpecZero` (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`),
18	but no relative projective space over an arbitrary base scheme.  Following the
19	`AffineSpace` pattern (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean`) and the
20	encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment `C-0002`), this file defines
21	
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace n S` (notation `ℙ(n; S)`): the relative
23	  projective space with homogeneous coordinates indexed by `n : Type u`, i.e.
24	  the pullback of the integral model
25	  `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n] = Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ))`
26	  along `S ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme`;
27	* the structural morphism `ℙ(n; S) ↘ S` (a `CanonicallyOver` instance) with
28	  `IsProper` (hence `IsSeparated`, `UniversallyClosed`, `LocallyOfFiniteType`,
29	  `QuasiCompact`) derived by base change from the Mathlib instances on
30	  `Proj.toSpecZero`;
31	* functoriality `ProjectiveSpace.map` in the base and the base-change square
32	  `ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map`.
33	
34	The key observations making the transfer work: the degree-zero part of the
35	homogeneous coordinate ring is the copy of `ULift ℤ` given by the constants
36	(`MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule_zero`), so `Spec (𝒜 0)` is terminal and
37	`terminal.from (Proj 𝒜)` factors as `Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜` followed by an
38	isomorphism; and for finitely many variables the coordinate ring is of finite
39	type over its degree-zero part, which is exactly the hypothesis of the Mathlib
40	properness instances.
41	
42	Blueprint: `def:projective_space`, `lem:projective_space_proper`
43	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
44	-/

46	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial

48	noncomputable section

50	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

52	universe u

54	/-- The total-degree grading on the homogeneous coordinate ring
55	`ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]` of the integral model of projective space (with `ULift ℤ`
56	coefficients for universe polymorphism, as in `AffineSpace`). -/
57	local notation3 "𝒫[" n "]" => homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift ℤ)
58	
59	/-- The total-degree grading is a graded ring structure.  Mathlib deliberately
60	does not register `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a global instance (other
61	weightings of the same polynomial ring exist); for the fixed homogeneous
62	coordinate ring of projective space we register it project-wide. -/
63	instance (n : Type u) : GradedRing 𝒫[n] :=
64	  MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra
65	
66	variable (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u})
67	
68	/-- `ℙ(n; S)` is the projective space over `S` with homogeneous coordinates
69	indexed by `n : Type u` (e.g. `ULift (Fin (m + 1))` for `ℙ^m_S`).  It is the
70	base change to `S` of the integral model `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]`. -/
71	def ProjectiveSpace (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u}) : Scheme.{u} :=
72	  pullback (terminal.from S)
73	    (terminal.from (Proj (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
74	
75	namespace ProjectiveSpace
76	
77	/-- `ℙ(n; S)` is the projective `n`-space over `S`. -/
78	scoped[AlgebraicGeometry] notation "ℙ(" n "; " S ")" => ProjectiveSpace n S
79	
80	instance canonicallyOver : (ℙ(n; S)).CanonicallyOver S where
81	  hom := pullback.fst _ _
82	
83	lemma over_eq_fst : ℙ(n; S) ↘ S = pullback.fst _ _ := rfl
84	
85	/-- The projection from `ℙ(n; S)` to the integral model `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ : i ∈ n]`. -/
86	def toProjInt : ℙ(n; S) ⟶ Proj 𝒫[n] := pullback.snd _ _
87	
88	lemma toProjInt_eq_snd : toProjInt n S = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

91	lemma over_terminal_comp :
92	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) ≫ terminal.from S = toProjInt n S ≫ terminal.from (Proj 𝒫[n]) :=
93	  pullback.condition

97	/-- The degree-zero part of the homogeneous coordinate ring is the copy of
98	`ULift ℤ` given by the constants. -/
99	lemma bijective_algebraMap_gradeZero :
100	    Function.Bijective
101	      (algebraMap (ULift.{u} ℤ) (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0)) := by
102	  constructor
103	  · intro a b hab

106	  · intro x

108	      ((MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule_zero (σ := n) (R := ULift.{u} ℤ)).le x.2)
109	    exact ⟨y, Subtype.ext (by simpa using hy)⟩

111	/-- The degree-zero part of the homogeneous coordinate ring, as a ring, is
112	`ULift ℤ`. -/
113	def gradeZeroRingEquiv :
114	    ULift.{u} ℤ ≃+* homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0 :=
115	  RingEquiv.ofBijective
116	    (algebraMap (ULift.{u} ℤ) (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0))
117	    (bijective_algebraMap_gradeZero n)
118	
119	/-- `Spec` of the degree-zero part of the homogeneous coordinate ring is a
120	terminal scheme. -/
121	def specGradeZeroIsTerminal :
122	    IsTerminal (Spec (.of (homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ) 0))) :=
123	  specULiftZIsTerminal.{u}.ofIso
124	    (Scheme.Spec.mapIso (gradeZeroRingEquiv n).toCommRingCatIso.op).symm

128	  isIso_of_isTerminal (specGradeZeroIsTerminal n) terminalIsTerminal _

/-- Given `f ∣ x`, this is the map `A_{(f)} → A_f → A_x`. We will lift this to a map

private def awayMapAux (hx : f ∣ x) : Away 𝒜 f →+* Localization.Away x :=

lemma awayMapAux_mk (n a i hi) :

      Localization.mk (a * g ^ i) ⟨x ^ i, (Submonoid.mem_powers_iff _ _).mpr ⟨i, rfl⟩⟩ := by
  have : algebraMap A (Localization.Away x) f *
    (Localization.mk g ⟨f * g, (Submonoid.mem_powers_iff _ _).mpr ⟨1, by simp [hx]⟩⟩) = 1 := by
    rw [← Algebra.smul_def, Localization.smul_mk]
    exact Localization.mk_self ⟨f*g, _⟩
  simp only [awayMapAux, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, algebraMap_apply, val_mk]

def awayMap : Away 𝒜 f →+* Away 𝒜 x := by
  let e := RingEquiv.ofLeftInverse (f := algebraMap (Away 𝒜 x) (Localization.Away x))
    (h := (val_injective _).hasLeftInverse.choose_spec)
  refine RingHom.comp (e.symm.toRingHom.comp (Subring.inclusion ?_))
    (awayMapAux 𝒜 (f := f) ⟨_, hx⟩).rangeRestrict

a field, `X ×[Y] Spec K` is integral. -/
@[mk_iff]
class GeometricallyIntegral (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop where
  geometrically_isIntegral : geometrically IsIntegral f

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometrically :
    @GeometricallyIntegral = geometrically IsIntegral := by
  ext; exact geometricallyIntegral_iff _

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible :
    @GeometricallyIntegral =
      (@GeometricallyReduced ⊓ @GeometricallyIrreducible : MorphismProperty Scheme) := by
  rw [eq_geometrically, GeometricallyReduced.eq_geometrically,
    GeometricallyIrreducible.eq_geometrically, ← geometrically_inf]
  eta_expand
  simp [isIntegral_iff_irreducibleSpace_and_isReduced, and_comm]

instance (priority := low) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyReduced f :=
  (GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible.le _ _ _ ‹_›).1

instance (priority := low) [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyIrreducible f :=
  (GeometricallyIntegral.eq_geometricallyReduced_inf_geometricallyIrreducible.le _ _ _ ‹_›).2

lemma GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible

instance [GeometricallyIntegral f] : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.snd f g) :=

/-!
# The Laurent chart pair on the projective line

Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1`: the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` of the two standard
charts of `P1 k` and its identification with the Laurent polynomial ring, the section-level
chart identifications, and the bundled chart package.

* `P1.overlapAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(X₀X₁))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[T,T⁻¹]`, with the two restriction maps
  `P1.awayToOverlapLeft/Right` becoming `t ↦ T` and `t ↦ T⁻¹`
  (`P1.overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft`/`Right`);
* the *Laurent span* property `P1.exists_awayToOverlap_add`: every element of the overlap
  ring is a sum of restrictions from the two charts;
* section-level versions of all of the above (`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀/₁`,
  `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`, `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_res_left/right`);
* the package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` with canonical term
  `P1.laurentChartPair k`, and the span property `LaurentChartPair.exists_res_add_res`
  for any such package. This package is exactly what the two-lattice finiteness argument
  for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
-/

/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₀)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
noncomputable def awayToOverlapLeft :
    Away 𝒜 (X 0) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1) rfl

/-- The restriction map from the chart `D₊(X₁)` to the overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`. -/
noncomputable def awayToOverlapRight :
    Away 𝒜 (X 1) →+* Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
  awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 0) (mul_comm (X 0) (X 1))

theorem awayToOverlapLeft_eq :
    awayToOverlapLeft k = awayMap 𝒜 (X_mem k 1)
      (rfl : (X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) * X 1 = X 0 * X 1) :=
  rfl

A locally trivial line bundle is invertible-graded (`IsLocallyTrivial.isInvertibleGr`,
the P0.5 bridge of `Picard/InvertibleGrBridge.lean`): the trivialising affine charts
form the required basis and each carries an invertible section module.  This upgrades
the Serre-twist family from `IsLocallyTrivial` to `Scheme.Modules.IsInvertibleGr`,
unlocking the graded-commutative section ring `Γ_*(X, O(m))`
(`sectionGradedRing_gcommSemiring`). -/

/-- **The glued Serre twist is invertible-graded** (P0.5). -/
instance serreTwistGlued_isInvertibleGr (m : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsInvertibleGr (serreTwistGlued n₀ m) :=
  (serreTwistGlued_isLocallyTrivial n₀ m).isInvertibleGr

/-- **`O(m)` on the integral model `Proj ℤ[X]` is invertible-graded** (P0.5). -/
instance serreTwist_isInvertibleGr (m : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsInvertibleGr (serreTwist n₀ m) :=
  (serreTwist_isLocallyTrivial n₀ m).isInvertibleGr

/-- **The relative twisting sheaf `O(m)` on `ℙ(n₀; S)` is invertible-graded** (P0.5). -/
instance twistingSheaf_isInvertibleGr (S : Scheme.{0}) (m : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsInvertibleGr (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n₀ S m) :=
  (twistingSheaf_isLocallyTrivial n₀ S m).isInvertibleGr

/-- **The section graded ring `Γ_*(Proj ℤ[X], O(m))` is graded-commutative** (P0.5):
the payoff of `IsInvertibleGr`, assembling a genuine `CommSemiring` on
`⊕_k Γ(Proj ℤ[X], O(m)^{⊗k})`. -/
example (m : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (CommSemiring (DirectSum ℕ (Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg (serreTwist n₀ m)))) :=
  Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedRing_commSemiring_nonempty (serreTwist n₀ m)

end LocallyTrivial

/-! ## Base change of `O(m)`-sections over a flat affine base (P0.2κ)

Over a **flat affine** base `S → Spec ℤ`, the global sections of the relative
Serre twist base-change: `Γ(S) ⊗_ℤ Γ(Proj ℤ[X], O(m)) ≅ Γ(ℙ(n₀; S), O(m))`.
This is the H⁰ flat base change (Stacks 02KE), applied to the cartesian square

```
ℙ(n₀; S) --toProjInt--> Proj ℤ[X]
   | ↘S                   | (to Spec ℤ = ⊤)
   S ---------------->  ⊤_ Scheme
```

at `V = U = ⊤`.  The bottom map `Proj → ⊤` is proper hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated (P0.4 makes `O(m)` quasi-coherent — the last hypothesis of the
